blocks.html: Hudson, WI · Adults 21+
From Hudson, it's about 10 minutes to licensed cannabis in Bayport

Hey, I'm Brandon. My Dealer is a state-licensed cannabis store in Bayport, Minnesota, just across the St. Croix from Hudson. Adults 21+ with a valid ID, including a Wisconsin license, can shop here. The catch is simple: buy it in Minnesota and use it in Minnesota.
First, the rule: buy in Minnesota, use it in Minnesota

I'd rather lose a sale than have you get in trouble, so this goes first. What you buy at My Dealer is legal in Minnesota only. Don't carry cannabis across state lines, and that includes the I-94 bridge back to Hudson. Wisconsin treats THC (outside of legal hemp) as a controlled substance, and Hudson has its own possession ordinance on top of state law. Every package we sell says it: "This product may be unlawful outside the state of Minnesota."

So plan where you'll use it on this side of the river before you come: a private residence, or private property where the owner is fine with it. Not in the car, not in a park, not in our lot. Our guide for Wisconsin shoppers has the statutes, the Hudson and St. Croix County ordinances, and the rest of the detail.
Local rules in Hudson and North Hudson

City of Hudson Code Chapter 118 (amended in full August 19, 2024) bans possessing or using marijuana, with a forfeiture of $50 to $500 plus costs. For more than 25 grams, or after a prior conviction, the city can cite you only if the St. Croix County District Attorney declines to charge. The same chapter makes it illegal for anyone under 21 to possess hemp-derived THC products such as delta-8 or THCA. Hudson Code ch. 118

St. Croix County Chapter 58 also bans marijuana possession (up to 25 grams, first offense), with a forfeiture of $125 to $500. St. Croix County ch. 58 (PDF) The Village of North Hudson's code (Sec. 70-12) also prohibits marijuana possession or use; we haven't verified its fine. North Hudson code State law applies on top of all of these.

In Bayport, City Code Sec. 26-77 (Ordinance 891, adopted August 7, 2023) bans smoking cannabis or hemp products in public places, and Sec. 26-28 bans open containers of cannabis or hemp drinks on streets, sidewalks, and other public places. Bayport Code ch. 26
Getting here from Hudson
From downtown Hudson

Take Second Street (Highway 35) up to I-94 and head west across the St. Croix. Take exit 258, the first exit on the Minnesota side, for Highway 95 toward Lakeland and Stillwater. Go north on 95 about 4 miles, through Lakeland and Lakeland Shores. In Bayport, we're on your right at 243 3rd St N, next to the American Legion and the post office and across from City Hall.
About 10 minutes, 5.7 miles. From North Hudson, about 13 minutes.
The I-94 bridges over the St. Croix are under repair in 2026. I-94 has stayed open, with lane shifts. Check 511 Wisconsin's project page for current traffic impacts.
From Houlton or farther north
Cross on the St. Croix Crossing (Highway 64 into Minnesota Highway 36), take the first exit for Highway 95, and head south. About 7 minutes from Houlton.
Drive time and distance: OpenStreetMap routing (OSRM), checked October 22, 2026, without traffic. Allow extra time when traffic is heavy.
Licensed cannabis vs. a hemp shop

There are shops on the Wisconsin side that call themselves dispensaries. They sell hemp-derived products, which is a different, lower-potency category with different rules. My Dealer is licensed by the Minnesota Office of Cannabis Management as a cannabis retailer (license DIS-L24-000241), and our flower is grown as cannabis by licensed Minnesota cultivators and tracked by the state. We carry some hemp-derived products too, and those are labeled as hemp. You can look our license up on OCM's list.
Hemp THC on December 11: what changes, and what doesn't

Heads up for Wisconsin shoppers looking for cannabis near Hudson. Under current federal law, starting December 11, 2026, a finished hemp product with more than 0.4 mg of total THC per package (the can, bottle, or bag it's sold in) no longer meets the federal definition of hemp. So do hemp products made with lab-converted cannabinoids. That covers most hemp THC gummies, vapes, and drinks, including delta-8. This is a federal change, not a new Wisconsin law. Wisconsin's hemp law hasn't changed, and two Wisconsin bills to regulate hemp THC products, AB 747 and SB 682, did not pass.

Minnesota has its own hemp law. The Minnesota Office of Cannabis Management says the federal change doesn't change how Minnesota defines lower-potency hemp edibles and drinks, or whether they're legal under Minnesota law. OCM also notes that many hemp products that comply with Minnesota law, such as packages with more than 0.4 mg of THC, won't meet the new federal definition, which could affect hemp businesses' banking, taxes, and interstate shipping.

Licensed Minnesota cannabis was never hemp. It's what most people mean by real weed: grown as cannabis by licensed Minnesota cultivators, tested, and tracked by the state. It's legal under Minnesota law only, and it's still illegal under federal law and in Wisconsin. Come visit Bayport, about 10 minutes from Hudson. Everything you buy here, cannabis or hemp, is for use in Minnesota only.

Our read, not legal advice. Sources: 7 U.S.C. 1639o as amended by P.L. 119-37, Div. B, Sec. 781 (enacted November 12, 2025); timing under P.L. 119-103, Sec. 2019 (signed September 2, 2026); Congressional Research Service IF13136; Minnesota OCM, Federal hemp changes; Wisconsin AB 747 and SB 682. Congress could still change these dates. Bills to delay the change again are in committee; as of October 22, 2026, none has passed.
Where Wisconsin cannabis law stands

As of October 22, 2026, Wisconsin has no adult-use or medical cannabis program. In the 2025-2026 session, lawmakers introduced a medical cannabis bill, a legalization bill, and several bills to regulate hemp THC products. None passed; all failed on March 23, 2026, under the session schedule, after the last regular floor period ended in mid-March. The Wisconsin shoppers guide lists each bill, its sponsors, and how to reach your legislators.
What we carry

New to cannabis? Deli flower, a single pre-roll, or a low-dose edible are easy places to start, and a budtender can walk you through any of them. Come visit Bayport and you'll find a wide range of brands, many of them from Minnesota, including RYTHM, Dogwalkers, Good Green, &Shine, Vireo, Campfire Cannabis, Flör, BLNCD, Minny Grown, Foundry, Granny's, and Philotimo, plus Trawa flower at the deli counter. Deli flower: ounces from $210, about 10 minutes from Hudson

Searching for a dispensary near Hudson, or for budget-friendly ounces near Hudson? Deli flower is the reason I'd point you over the bridge. It's weighed to order at the counter on certified scales, right in front of you, so you pick the amount, from a single gram up to two ounces, the Minnesota limit for one purchase. Mixing strains within a tier still counts toward the bulk price.

Ounces run $210 or $225 depending on the tier. The more you buy, the less each gram costs. In the $11 tier, a single gram is $11, 3.5 g works out to $10.00 a gram, 14 g to $8.57 a gram, and a full ounce to $7.50 a gram. The $12 tier steps down the same way, to $8.04 a gram at the ounce. Same rule as everything else here: it stays in Minnesota, so plan where you'll use it on this side of the river.

Your first visit
Your Wisconsin ID works. So does any other valid ID on this list.

items: 21+ with a valid ID, every visit. A driver's license or state ID from any U.S. state works, and so do a Canadian license or ID, a Tribal ID, a U.S. passport or passport card, or a foreign passport. No one under 21 can come in, even with an adult.
Paying: cash, or your debit card through our cashless ATM ($3 fee). There's a regular ATM on site too. No credit cards.
Loyalty: give us your phone number at checkout and you earn 3% back in points, plus access to member deals.
Discounts: veterans and active military get 15% off every day, and Andersen employees get 10% off on Tuesdays, with valid ID. Discounts don't stack; you get the best one for your cart.
Limits: Minnesota caps one purchase at 2 ounces of flower, 8 grams of concentrate (vapes count here), and 800 mg of THC in edibles and hemp THC products combined.
No consumption on site. We're a retail store only, and there's no place to use cannabis at My Dealer.
